verses.1:1: And in the first year of Cyrus the king of the Persians, that it might be fulfilled from the mouth of Jeremiah, He stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of the Persians, and he sent forth a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and also in writing, saying,
verses.1:2: "Thus says Cyrus king of the Persians: The God of heaven has given to me all the kingdoms, and He Himself has charged me to build Him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.
verses.1:3: Who is among you of all His people? And his God shall be with him, and he shall go up to Jerusalem.
verses.1:4: And everyone who remains from all the places where he sojourns, the men of his place shall support him with silver and gold, and with goods and livestock, together with the freewill offering for the house of the God who is in Jerusalem."
verses.1:5: Then the heads of the fathers' houses of Judah and Benjamin arose, and the priests and the Levites, with all whose spirit God had stirred up, to go up to build the house which is in Jerusalem.
verses.1:6: And all those around them strengthened their hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with goods, and with livestock, and with precious gifts, besides the freewill offerings.
verses.1:7: And King Cyrus brought forth the vessels of the house, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem and had placed in the house of his god.
verses.1:8: And Cyrus king of the Persians brought them forth by the hand of Mithredath the Tasbarene, and counted them out to Sabanasar, prince of Judah.
verses.1:9: And this is the number of them: for the Lord, thirty of gold and one thousand of silver, twenty-nine replacements,
verses.1:10: thirty bowls of gold and six of silver, and one thousand other vessels.
verses.1:11: All the vessels of gold and of silver were five thousand four hundred, all of them going up from the captivity out of Babylon to Jerusalem.
verses.2:1: Now these are the sons of the province who came up out of the captivity of the exile, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away into Babylon, and returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each man to his own city.
verses.2:2: Those who came with Zerubbabel were Jeshua, Nehemiah, Araiah, Reelaiah, Marathchai, Baspham, Malsar, Batusi, and Balleia. The number of the men of Israel:
verses.2:3: The sons of Phares, two thousand one hundred and seventy-two;
verses.2:4: And the sons of Asaph, four hundred and seventy-two;
verses.2:5: The sons of Era, seven hundred and seventy-five;
verses.2:6: The sons of Phalab-Moab, of the sons of Jeshua and Jobab, two thousand eight hundred and twelve;
verses.2:7: The sons of Malam, one thousand two hundred and fifty-four;
verses.2:8: The sons of Zathua, nine hundred and forty-five;
verses.2:9: The sons of Zacchu, seven hundred and sixty;
verses.2:10: The sons of Banu, six hundred and forty-two;
verses.2:11: The sons of Bebai, six hundred and twenty-three;
verses.2:12: The sons of Azgad, three thousand two hundred and twenty-two;
verses.2:13: The sons of Adonikam, six hundred and sixty-six;
verses.2:14: The sons of Baogei, two thousand and fifty-six;
verses.2:15: The sons of Adin, four hundred and fifty-four;
verses.2:16: The sons of Ater, of Hezekiah, ninety-two;
verses.2:17: The sons of Basu, three hundred and twenty-three;
verses.2:18: The sons of Ura, one hundred and twelve;
verses.2:19: The sons of Hashum, two hundred and twenty-three;
verses.2:21: The sons of Barthaleem, one hundred and twenty-three;
verses.2:23: The sons of Anathoth, one hundred and twenty-eight;
verses.2:25: The sons of Kiriath-Jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, seven hundred and forty-three;
verses.2:26: The sons of Haram and Geba, six hundred and twenty-one;
verses.2:27: The men of Michmash, one hundred and twenty-two;
verses.2:28: The men of Gaithel and Ai, two hundred and twenty-three;
verses.2:30: The sons of Magebos, one hundred and fifty-six;
verses.2:31: The sons of Elamar, two thousand two hundred and fifty-four;
verses.2:32: The sons of Harim, three hundred and twenty;
verses.2:33: The sons of Lod, Haroth, and Ono, six hundred and twenty-five;
verses.2:34: The sons of Jereia, three hundred and forty-five;
verses.2:35: The sons of Senaah, three thousand six hundred and thirty.
verses.2:36: And the priests: the sons of Jeuda, of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred and seventy-three;
verses.2:37: The sons of Immer, one thousand and fifty-two;
verses.2:38: The sons of Pashhur, one thousand two hundred and forty-seven;
verses.2:39: The sons of Harim, one thousand and seven.
verses.2:40: And the Levites: the sons of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the sons of Soduia, seventy-four;
verses.2:41: The singers: the sons of Asaph, one hundred and forty-eight;
verses.2:42: The sons of the gates: the sons of Shallum, the sons of Ater, the sons of Talmon, the sons of Akum, the sons of Hatita, the sons of Abau, in all one hundred and thirty-nine.
verses.2:43: The Nethinim: the sons of Suthia, the sons of Hasupha, the sons of Tabbaoth,
verses.2:44: the sons of Kades, the sons of Soel, the sons of Padon,
verses.2:45: the sons of Labano, the sons of Hagabah, the sons of Akaboth,
verses.2:46: the sons of Hagab, the sons of Samaan, the sons of Hanan,
verses.2:47: the sons of Keded, the sons of Gael, the sons of Reel,
verses.2:48: the sons of Rason, the sons of Nekoda, the sons of Gazzam,
verses.2:49: the sons of Uzza, the sons of Phison, the sons of Besai,
verses.2:50: the sons of Asnah, the sons of Manoemein, the sons of Napheison,
verses.2:51: the sons of Bakkuk, the sons of Hapheika, the sons of Harhur,
verses.2:52: the sons of Basadoe, the sons of Mauda, the sons of Harsha,
verses.2:53: the sons of Barkos, the sons of Temah,
verses.2:54: the sons of Nasus, the sons of Hatupha,
verses.2:55: the sons of Abdesel, the sons of Sotai, the sons of Hassophereth, the sons of Phadura,
verses.2:56: the sons of Jaalah, the sons of Darkon, the sons of Gedea,
verses.2:57: the sons of Shephatiah, the sons of Hateia, the sons of Phasrath, the sons of Haseboein, the sons of Emei.
verses.2:58: All the Nethinim and the sons of Asedeselma were three hundred and seventy-two.
verses.2:59: And these are the ones who came up from Thermeleth, Thaaresa, Charus, Edan, and Immer; and they could not declare their father's house and their lineage, whether they were in Israel:
verses.2:60: The sons of Lachea, the sons of Bua, the sons of Tobiah, the sons of Nekoda, six hundred and fifty-two.
verses.2:61: And of the sons of the priests: the sons of Labeia, the sons of Hakkoz, the sons of Zarbelthei, who took a wife from the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called by their name.
verses.2:62: These, the Methoeseim, sought their register, and they were not found, and they were removed from the priesthood.
verses.2:63: And Athersaa said to them that they should not eat of the most holy things until a priest should arise with the Lights and the Perfections.
verses.2:64: Now the whole assembly was about forty-two thousand three hundred and sixty,
verses.2:65: besides their servants and maidservants—these were seven thousand three hundred and thirty-four; and these, singers and songs, were two hundred.
verses.2:66: Their horses were seven hundred and thirty, and their mules two hundred and forty-five;
verses.2:67: their camels were four hundred and thirty-five; their donkeys were seven hundred and twenty.
verses.2:68: And some of the rulers of the fathers' houses, when they came to the house of the Lord which is in Jerusalem, offered freely for the house of God, to set it up on its prepared place.
verses.2:69: According to their ability, they gave to the treasury of the work pure gold, sixty-one thousand minas; and five thousand minas of silver; and one hundred tunics of the priests.
verses.2:70: And the priests and the Levites, and some of the people, and the singers, and the gatekeepers, and the Thanieim dwelt in their cities, and all Israel in their cities.
verses.3:1: And the seventh month arrived, and those of Israel were in their cities; then the people gathered together as one man to Jerusalem.
verses.3:2: Then Jeshua the son of Jozadak and his brethren arose and built the altar of the God of Israel, to offer burnt offerings on it, according to what is written in the law of Moses, the man of God.
verses.3:3: And they set the altar upon its prepared base, and a burnt offering went up upon it to the Lord in the morning and toward evening.
verses.3:4: They also kept the Feast of Tabernacles as it is written, with burnt offerings day by day in number according to the ordinance, the daily portion for each day;
verses.3:5: and afterward the continual burnt offerings, both for the new moons and for all the consecrated feasts, and for everyone who willingly presented a freewill offering to the Lord.
verses.3:6: On the first day of the seventh month they began to offer burnt offerings to the Lord, though the house of the Lord had not been founded.
verses.3:7: They also gave silver to the stonecutters and to the carpenters, and food, drink, and oil to the Sedamein and to the Sorein, to bring cedar timber from Lebanon to the sea of Joppa, according to the grant of Cyrus king of the Persians to them.
verses.3:8: Now in the second year of their coming to the house of God at Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and the rest of the brethren, the priests and the Levites, and all who came from the captivity to Jerusalem, made a beginning and appointed the Levites from twenty years old and above over the works of the Lord.
verses.3:9: Then Jeshua and his sons and his brethren, Kadmiel and his sons, the sons of Judah, stood over those doing the work in the house of God—the sons of Henaad, their sons and their brethren, the Levites.
verses.3:10: And they laid the foundation to build the house of the Lord; and the priests stood vested with trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, to praise the Lord according to the direction of David king of Israel.
verses.3:11: And they responded in praise and thanksgiving to the Lord, "For it is good, for His mercy is forever upon Israel." And all the people raised a great shout to praise the Lord at the laying of the foundation of the house of the Lord.
verses.3:12: Yet many of the priests and the Levites and heads of the fathers' houses, the elders who had seen the first house at its foundation, and saw this house before their eyes, wept with a loud voice; while a multitude shouted with gladness to lift up a song.
verses.3:13: And the people could not distinguish the sound of the shout of gladness from the sound of the weeping, for the people cried out with a loud voice, and it was heard even from afar.
verses.4:1: Now those who afflicted Judah and Benjamin heard that the sons of the captivity were building a house for the Lord God of Israel.
verses.4:2: And they drew near to Zerubbabel and to the heads of the fathers' houses, and said to them, "We will build with you, for like you we seek our God, and to Him we have been sacrificing since the days of Asareathon king of Assyria, who brought us here."
verses.4:3: But Zerubbabel and Jeshua and the rest of the heads of the fathers' houses of Israel said to them, "It is not for us and for you to build a house for our God; for we ourselves together will build for the Lord our God, as Cyrus king of the Persians commanded us."
verses.4:4: Then the people of the land kept weakening the hands of the people of Judah, and they hindered them from building,
verses.4:5: and hiring others against them, seeking to frustrate their counsel, all the days of Cyrus king of the Persians and until the reign of Darius king of the Persians.
verses.4:6: And in the reign of Astherou, at the beginning of his reign, he wrote against those who dwelt in Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.4:7: And in the days of Asarthatha, Tabeel wrote in peace to Mithredath and to the rest of the fellow servants; to the king of the Persians the tax collector wrote a document in the Syrian tongue, and translated.
verses.4:8: Raoul Badatamen and Samasa the scribe wrote one letter against Jerusalem to King Arsartha.
verses.4:9: Thus decreed Raoum Baal and Samee the scribe and the rest of our fellow servants, the Dinaites, the Pharesthachites, the Taraphallites, the Aphrasites, the Archuites, the Babylonians, the Susunachites who are Elamites,
verses.4:10: and the rest of the nations whom Asennaphar the great and honorable deported and settled in the cities of Somoron and the remainder beyond the River.
verses.4:11: This is the copy of the letter which they sent to him: "To King Arsartha, your servants, the men beyond the River.
verses.4:12: Let it be known to the king that the Jews who came up from Cyrus have come to us to Jerusalem; they are building that rebellious and wicked city, and have restored its walls, and have raised up its foundations.
verses.4:13: Now therefore let it be known to the king that if that city is built and its walls are restored, there will be no tribute for you, nor will they pay it; and this harms kings.
verses.4:14: And it is not fitting for us to behold the dishonor of the king; therefore we have sent and informed the king,
verses.4:15: that search may be made in the book of the records of your fathers; and you will find and know that that city is a rebellious city, bringing harm to kings and provinces, and that places of refuge for slaves have been in its midst from days of old; for these reasons this city was laid waste.
verses.4:16: We inform the king that if that city is built and its walls are restored, there is no peace for you."
verses.4:17: Then the king sent peace to Raoum Balgam and Sameais the scribe and the rest of their fellow servants who dwelt in Samaria, and to the rest beyond the River, saying,
verses.4:18: "The tax collector whom you sent to us was summoned before me.
verses.4:19: And a decree was issued by me, and we searched and found that from days of old that city has lifted itself up against kings, and rebellions and places of refuge occur in it.
verses.4:20: And mighty kings arise over Jerusalem, ruling over all the west of the River, and full tribute and a portion are given to them.
verses.4:21: Now issue a decree to stop those men, and that city shall no longer be built from this decree.
verses.4:22: Be on your guard against showing negligence concerning this, lest destruction multiply to the harm of kings."
verses.4:23: Then the tax collector of King Arsartha read before Raoum and Samesa the scribe and their fellow servants; and they went in haste to Jerusalem and into Judah, and stopped them with horses and force.
verses.4:24: Then the work of the house of God which is in Jerusalem ceased, and it remained at a standstill until the second year of Darius king of the Persians.
verses.5:1: Then Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo prophesied a prophecy to the Jews who were in Judah and Jerusalem, in the name of the God of Israel who was over them.
verses.5:2: So Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and Jeshua the son of Jozadak arose and began to build the house of God which is in Jerusalem; and with them were the prophets of God, helping them.
verses.5:3: At that same time Thananai, the governor beyond the River, and Satharbouzana and their fellow servants came to them and spoke thus to them: "Who issued a decree for you to build the house and to complete this furnishing?"
verses.5:4: Then they said these things to them: "What are the names of the men who are building this city?"
verses.5:5: But the eyes of God were upon the captivity of Judah, and they did not stop them until a report was brought to Darius; and then it was sent to the tax collector concerning this matter.
verses.5:6: The copy of the letter which Thanthanas, governor of the region beyond, and Satharbouzana and their fellow servants, the Apharsachites beyond the River, sent to King Darius;
verses.5:7: they sent a report to him, and thus it was written in it:
verses.5:8: "To King Darius, all peace. Let it be known to the king that we went into the province of Judea, to the house of the great God; and it is being built with choice stones, and timber is being laid in the walls, and that work is going forward skillfully and prospering in their hands.
verses.5:9: Then we questioned those elders and spoke thus to them: 'Who issued a decree for you to build this furnishing and to complete it?'
verses.5:10: We also asked them for their names to inform you, so that we might write down the names of the men who were their leaders.
verses.5:11: And this word they answered us, saying, 'We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth, and we are building the house that was built many years before this; and a great king of Israel built it and completed it for them.
verses.5:12: But since our fathers provoked the God of heaven to wrath, He gave them into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he destroyed this house and carried the people away captive to Babylon.
verses.5:13: However, in the first year of Cyrus the king, King Cyrus issued a decree that this house of God should be built.
verses.5:14: Also the silver and gold vessels of God, which Nebuchadnezzar had brought out from the house that was in Jerusalem and carried to the temple of the king, these he gave to Bagasar the treasurer, who was over the treasury,
verses.5:15: and said to him, "Take all the vessels; go, put them in the house that is in Jerusalem, in their own place."
verses.5:16: Then that Sarbagar came and laid the foundations of the house of God which is in Jerusalem; and from that time until now it has been in building, and has not been finished.'
verses.5:17: And now, if it seems good to the king, let a search be made in the treasure house of the king of Babylon, so that you may know that a decree was issued by King Cyrus to build that house of God which is in Jerusalem; and when the king has learned concerning this matter, let him send to us."
verses.6:1: Then Darius the king issued a decree, and he made search in the archives where the treasure is laid up in Babylon.
verses.6:2: And there was found in the city, in the fortress, one scroll, and this memorandum was written in it:
verses.6:3: "In the first year of Cyrus the king, Cyrus the king issued a decree concerning the holy house of God which is in Jerusalem, and the place where they offer the sacrifices. And he set an elevation, sixty cubits in height,
verses.6:4: and three courses of stone, and one course of timber; and the expense shall be given from the house of the king.
verses.6:5: And the vessels of the house of God, of silver and of gold, which Nebuchadnezzar brought out from the house which is in Jerusalem, were set in their place in the house of God."
verses.6:6: "Now you shall give, O governors beyond the River, Shethar-Boznai and their fellow servants the Apharsachites beyond the River, keeping far away from there:
verses.6:7: leave alone the work of the house of God; and let the elders of the Jews build that house of God in its place.
verses.6:8: And by me a decree has been issued lest you ever do anything with the elders of the Jews for the building of that house of God; and from the possessions of the king, of the tribute beyond the River, let the expense be diligently given to those men, so that they may not be hindered.
verses.6:9: And whatever is lacking—both young bulls and rams and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, wheat, salt, wine, and oil, according to the word of the priests who are in Jerusalem—let it be given to them day by day, whatever they may ask,
verses.6:10: that they may offer sweet aromas to the God of heaven, and pray for the life of the king and of his sons.
verses.6:11: Also by me a decree has been issued that every man who alters this word, a timber shall be pulled down from his house, and being set upright he shall be struck upon it; and his house shall be dealt with according to my will.
verses.6:12: And the God whose name dwells there shall overthrow every king and people who stretches out his hand to alter or to destroy the house of God which is in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have issued a decree; it shall be done diligently."
verses.6:13: Then Tattenai, governor beyond the River, Shethar-Boznai, and his fellow servants, according to what Darius the king had sent, so they diligently did.
verses.6:14: And the elders of the Jews and the Levites were building through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo; and they built and finished it by the decree of the God of Israel, and by the decree of Cyrus, and Darius, and Artaxerxes, kings of the Persians.
verses.6:15: And they finished this house by the third day of the month of Adar, which was the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king.
verses.6:16: And the children of Israel, the priests and the Levites and the rest of the children of the captivity, kept the dedication of the house of God with gladness.
verses.6:17: And they offered at the dedication of the house of God one hundred young bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, and as a sin offering for all Israel twelve male goats, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
verses.6:18: And they appointed the priests in their division and the Levites in their courses for the service of God who is in Jerusalem, according to the writing of the book of Moses.
verses.6:19: And the children of the captivity kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
verses.6:20: For the priests and the Levites had purified themselves; all of them to a man were clean; and they slaughtered the Passover for all the children of the captivity, and for their brethren the priests, and for themselves.
verses.6:21: And the children of Israel who were from the captivity ate the Passover, together with everyone who separated himself with respect to the uncleannesses of the nations of the land to join them, to seek the Lord God of Israel.
verses.6:22: And they kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread seven days with gladness, for He made them glad, and the heart of the king of Assyria turned toward them, to strengthen their hands in the works of the house of the God of Israel.
verses.7:1: Now after these things, in the reign of Artaxerxes king of the Persians, Ezra went up, the son of Seraiah, the son of Zariah, the son of Hilkiah,
verses.7:2: the son of Shallum, the son of Zadok, the son of Ahitub,
verses.7:3: the son of Samariah, the son of Esriah, the son of Mareroth,
verses.7:4: the son of Zerahiah, the son of Saouia, the son of Bukki,
verses.7:5: the son of Abishua, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the ancestral priest.
verses.7:6: He went up from Babylon, and he was a ready scribe in the law of Moses, which the Lord God of Israel had given; and the king granted to him, because the hand of his God was upon him, in all that he sought.
verses.7:7: And some of the children of Israel, and of the priests, and of the Levites, and the singers, and the gatekeepers, and the Nethinim went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of Artaxerxes the king.
verses.7:8: And they came to Jerusalem in the fifth month; this was the seventh year of the king.
verses.7:9: For on the first day of the fifth month they came to Jerusalem, because the good hand of his God was upon him.
verses.7:10: For Ezra had set it in his heart to seek the law, and to do it, and to teach statutes and judgment in Israel.
verses.7:11: Now this is the copy of the decree which Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest, the scribe of the book of the words of the commandments of the Lord and of His statutes to Israel:
verses.7:12: "Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra, scribe of the law of the God of heaven: The matter and the reply have been completed.
verses.7:13: By me a decree has been issued that everyone in my kingdom who is willing, of the people of Israel and of the priests and Levites, to go to Jerusalem, may go with you.
verses.7:14: From the presence of the king and of the seven counselors it has been sent to make inquiry concerning Judea and Jerusalem, by the law of their God which is in your hand,
verses.7:15: and for the house of the Lord, silver and gold which the king and the counselors have freely offered to the Lord of Israel, who dwells in Jerusalem,
verses.7:16: and all the silver and gold that you may find in all the province of Babylon, together with the freewill offering of the people and of the priests who offer willingly for the house of God which is in Jerusalem.
verses.7:17: And everything that comes in, enter it promptly in this book: young bulls, rams, lambs, and their offerings and their drink offerings; and you shall offer them upon the altar of the house of your God which is in Jerusalem.
verses.7:18: And furthermore, has it seemed good to you and to your brethren to do anything with the rest of the silver and the gold? Do as is pleasing to your God.
verses.7:19: And the vessels that are given to you for the service of the house of God, deliver before God in Jerusalem.
verses.7:20: And the rest of the need of the house of God, whatever it may seem fit to you to give, you shall give from the treasure houses of the king.
verses.7:21: And from me—I myself, Artaxerxes the king—I have issued a decree to all the treasuries that are beyond the River, that whatever Ezra the priest, scribe of the law of the God of heaven, may ask of you, let it be done promptly,
verses.7:22: up to talents of silver, and up to one hundred kors of wheat, and up to one hundred storehouses of wine, and salt of which there is no written limit.
verses.7:23: Everything that is in the decree of the God of heaven, let it be done. Take heed lest you lay hands on anything against the house of the God of heaven, lest wrath come upon the kingdom of the king and of his sons.
verses.7:24: Also it is made known to you concerning all the priests and the Levites, singers, gatekeepers, Nethinim, and ministers of this house of God: let there be no tribute for you; you shall have no authority to bring them into bondage.
verses.7:25: And you, Ezra, in whose hand is the wisdom of God, appoint scribes and judges, that they may judge all the people who are beyond the River, all who know the law of God; and to him who does not know, you shall make it known.
verses.7:26: And everyone who does not promptly do the law of God and the law of the king, judgment shall be executed upon him, whether to death, or to chastisement, or to forfeiture of property, or to imprisonment."
verses.7:27: Blessed be the Lord God of our fathers, who has put such a thing in the heart of the king, who glorified the house which is in Jerusalem,
verses.7:28: and has extended mercy to me in the sight of the king and of his counselors, and of all the exalted princes of the king. And I was strengthened as the good hand of God was upon me, and I gathered leaders from Israel to go up with me.
verses.8:1: Now these are the leaders of their fathers' houses, the guides who went up with me in the reign of Artaxerxes the king of Babylon:
verses.8:2: of the sons of Phinehas, Gershom; of the sons of Ithamar, Daniel; of the sons of David, Tous;
verses.8:3: of the sons of Sanachia, of the sons of Parosh, Zechariah, and with him the company of one hundred and fifty;
verses.8:4: of the sons of Pahath-Moab, Eliana the son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred males;
verses.8:5: and of the sons of Zathoe, Shecaniah the son of Aziel, and with him three hundred males.
verses.8:6: And of the sons of Adin, Obeth the son of Jonathan, and with him fifty males;
verses.8:7: of the sons of Elah, Josiah the son of Atheli, and with him seventy males;
verses.8:8: of the sons of Shephatiah, Zebadiah the son of Michael, and with him eighty males;
verses.8:9: of the sons of Joab, Adiah the son of Iema, and with him two hundred and eighteen males;
verses.8:10: of the sons of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah, and with him one hundred and sixty males;
verses.8:11: and of the sons of Bebai, Azariah the son of Bebai, and with him seventy-eight males;
verses.8:12: of the sons of Astad, Johanan the son of Hakkatan, and with him one hundred and ten males;
verses.8:13: of the sons of Adonikam, the last ones, and these are their names: Eliphat, Euia, and Shemaiah, sixty males;
verses.8:14: and of the sons of Bago, Uthai, and with him eighty males.
verses.8:15: And I gathered them to the river that flows to Euim, and we encamped there three days. And I looked closely among the people and among the priests, and I found none of the sons of Levi there.
verses.8:16: Then I sent for the men Eleazar, Ariel, Shemaiah, Alonam, Areb, Elnatham, Nathan, Zechariah, and Mesuam, and for Arib and Eanathan, men of understanding.
verses.8:17: And I brought them out to the ruler in the silver of the place, and I put words in their mouth to speak to their brethren of the Athanim in the silver of the place, to bring us singers for the house of our God.
verses.8:18: And there came to us, as the good hand of our God was upon us, a man, Sachoch, of the sons of Mahli the son of Levi, the son of Israel; and at the beginning came his sons and his brethren, eighteen;
verses.8:19: and Hashabiah and Osaiah of the sons of Merari, his brethren and their sons, twenty;
verses.8:20: and of the Nethinim, whom David and the leaders had given for the service of the Levites, two hundred and twenty Nethinim; all of them were gathered by name.
verses.8:21: Then I proclaimed a fast there at the river Thue, that we might humble ourselves before our God, to seek from Him a straight way for us and for our children and for all our possessions.
verses.8:22: For I was ashamed to ask of the king an armed force and horsemen to save us from the enemy on the way, because we had spoken to the king, saying, "The hand of our God is upon all those who seek Him for good, and His power and His wrath are against all those who forsake Him."
verses.8:23: So we fasted and sought from our God concerning this matter, and He heard us.
verses.8:24: And I set apart twelve of the leaders of the priests: Seraiah, Hashabiah, and with them twelve of their brethren.
verses.8:25: And I weighed out to them the silver and the gold and the vessels, the offering of the house of our God, which the king and his counselors and his officials and all Israel who were found there had offered up.
verses.8:26: I weighed into their hands six hundred and fifty talents of silver, and one hundred silver vessels, and one hundred talents of gold;
verses.8:27: and twenty golden bowls, for the way one thousand chamaneim, and choice vessels of fine gleaming bronze, precious as gold.
verses.8:28: And I said to them, "You are holy to the Lord, and the vessels are holy, and the silver and the gold are freewill offerings to the Lord God of our fathers.
verses.8:29: Watch and keep guard until you stand before the leaders of the priests and the Levites and the leaders of the fathers' houses in Jerusalem, at the tents of the house of the Lord."
verses.8:30: So the priests and the Levites received the weight of the silver and the gold and the vessels, to bring them to Jerusalem to the house of our God.
verses.8:31: Then we departed from the river Thue on the twelfth day of the first month to go to Jerusalem. And the hand of our God was upon us, and He delivered us from the hand of the enemy and the adversary along the way.
verses.8:32: So we came to Jerusalem, and we remained there three days.
verses.8:33: Now it came to pass on the fourth day that we weighed out the silver and the gold and the vessels in the house of our God into the hand of Meremoth the son of Uriah the priest, and with him was Eleazar the son of Phinehas, and with them were Jozabad the son of Jeshua and Noadi of Ebannaia, the Levites—
verses.8:34: everything by number and by weight; and all the weight was written down.
verses.8:35: At that time, those who had come out of the captivity, the sons of the exile, offered burnt offerings to the God of Israel: twelve young bulls for all Israel, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve male goats for a sin offering—all of them as burnt offerings.
verses.8:36: And they delivered the king's decree to the king's administrators and to the governors beyond the River, and they honored the people and the house of God.
verses.9:1: Now when these things were finished, the leaders drew near to me, saying, "The people of Israel and the priests and the Levites have not separated themselves from the peoples of the lands in their abominations—those of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Jebusite, the Ammonite, Moab, the Moseri, and the Amorite.
verses.9:2: For they have taken some of their daughters for themselves and for their sons, so that the holy seed has been led astray among the peoples of the lands; and the hand of the leaders is in this unfaithfulness."
verses.9:3: And when I heard this word, I tore my garments and trembled, and I plucked out some of the hair of my head and of my beard, and sat down in silence.
verses.9:4: Then everyone who pursued the word of the God of Israel was gathered to me because of the unfaithfulness of the exile; and I sat in silence until the evening sacrifice.
verses.9:5: And at the evening sacrifice I arose from my humiliation; and having torn my garments, I trembled, and I bowed upon my knees and spread out my hands to God,
verses.9:6: and I said: "I am ashamed and humiliated to lift up my face to You, for our iniquities have multiplied above our head, and our trespasses have grown great even to heaven.
verses.9:7: From the days of our fathers we have been in great trespass to this day; and because of our iniquities we, our kings, and our sons have been delivered into the hand of the kings of the nations, to the sword and to captivity, to plunder and to shame of our face, as it is this day.
verses.9:8: And now our God has made provision for us to leave us for deliverance, and to give us a firm support in the place of His sanctuary, to enlighten our eyes and to give a little reviving in our bondage.
verses.9:9: For we are bondservants; yet in our bondage the Lord our God did not forsake us, and He inclined mercy toward us before the kings of Persia, to give us reviving, that they might raise up the house of our God and restore its desolate places, and to give us a hedge in Judah and in Jerusalem.
verses.9:10: What shall we say, O our God, after this? For we have forsaken Your commandments,
verses.9:11: which You gave us by the hand of Your servants the prophets: 'The land which you are entering to inherit is a land unsettled by the shifting of the peoples of the nations, in their abominations, with which they have filled it from mouth to mouth in their uncleannesses.
verses.9:12: Now therefore, do not give your daughters to their sons, nor take any of their daughters for your sons, and you shall not seek their peace or their good forever, that you may be strong and eat the good things of the land, and leave it as an inheritance to your sons forever.'
verses.9:13: And after all that has come upon you for your evil deeds and for your great trespass—for there is none like our God, because You have lightened our iniquities and have given us deliverance—
verses.9:14: because we have turned back to break Your commandments and to intermarry with the peoples, do not be provoked to anger against us to the point of utter destruction, so that there would be no remnant and no survivor.
verses.9:15: O Lord God of Israel, You are righteous, for we have been left as survivors, as it is this day. We are before You in our trespasses, for no one can stand before You because of this."
verses.10:1: Now as Ezra prayed, and as he confessed, weeping and praying before the house of God, a very great assembly from Israel was gathered to him, men and women and youths; for the people wept and lifted up their weeping.
verses.10:2: And Shecaniah the son of Jehiel, of the sons of Elam, answered and said to Ezra, "We have broken faith with our God and have caused foreign wives from the peoples of the land to dwell with us; yet now there is patient hope for Israel concerning this.
verses.10:3: Now therefore, let us make a covenant with our God to put away all the wives and those born of them, according as you desire; arise and put them in fear by the commandments of our God, and let it be done according to the law.
verses.10:4: Arise, for the matter rests upon you, and we are with you; be strong and act."
verses.10:5: Then Ezra arose and made the rulers, the Levites, and all Israel swear an oath to do according to this word; and they swore.
verses.10:6: And Ezra rose up from before the house of God and went into the treasury chamber of Johanan the son of Eliashib, and he went there; he ate no bread and drank no water, for he mourned over the faithlessness of the captivity.
verses.10:7: And they sent forth a proclamation to Judah and in Jerusalem,
verses.10:8: "Whoever does not come within three days, according to the counsel of the rulers and the elders, all his possessions shall be placed under the ban, and he himself shall be separated from the assembly of the captivity."
verses.10:9: Then all the men of Judah and Benjamin were gathered to Jerusalem within the three days; this was the ninth month. On the twentieth day of the month, all the people sat in the open square of the house of God, because of their agitation over the matter and because of the winter storm.
verses.10:10: And Ezra the priest arose and said to them, "You have broken faith and have caused foreign wives to dwell with you, to add to the trespass of Israel.
verses.10:11: Now therefore, give praise to the God of our fathers, and do what is pleasing before Him, and separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from the foreign wives."
verses.10:12: Then all the assembly answered and said, "Great is this word of yours for us to do.
verses.10:13: Yet the people are many, and the place is wintry, and there is no strength to stand outside; nor is the work for one day or for two, for we have greatly multiplied our wrongdoing in this matter.
verses.10:14: Let our rulers now stand; and for all those in our cities, whoever has caused foreign wives to dwell with him, let them come at appointed times from the gatherings, and with them the elders of every city and the judges, to turn away the fierce wrath of our God from us concerning this matter."
verses.10:15: Only Jonathan the son of Asahel and Lazeia the son of Hilkiah were with me concerning this, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite were helping them.
verses.10:16: And the sons of the captivity did so. And Ezra the priest and men who were heads of ancestral houses by house, and all of them by name, were set apart, for they returned on a day of the tenth month to examine the matter.
verses.10:17: And they finished with all the men who had caused foreign wives to dwell with them by the first day of the first month.
verses.10:18: Now among the sons of the priests who had caused foreign wives to dwell with them were found: of the sons of Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and his brethren: Meesel, Eliezer, Jarim, and Gedaliah.
verses.10:19: And they gave their hand to put away their wives, and for their trespass a ram from the flock concerning their guilt.
verses.10:20: And of the sons of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.
verses.10:21: And of the sons of Harim: Masael, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.
verses.10:22: And of the sons of Pashhur: Eliona, Maaseiah, Samael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah.
verses.10:23: And of the Levites: Jozabad, Samu, Kelaiah—that is, Kolieu—Pedaiah, Jodom, and Eliezer;
verses.10:24: and of the singers: Elisaph; and of the gatekeepers: Gellem, Telem, and Odouth.
verses.10:25: And of Israel, of the sons of Parosh: Ramiah, Aziah, Malchijah, Amamin, Eleazar, and Benaiah.
verses.10:26: And of the sons of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdiah, Jeremoth, and Elijah.
verses.10:27: And of the sons of Zathuia: Eliona, Eliashib, Alathaniah, Amon, Zabadab, and Uzziah.
verses.10:28: And of the sons of Bebai: Johanan, Niana, Zabu, and Thali.
verses.10:29: And of the sons of Banui: Melusham, Alum, Ada, Jasud, Shaluiah, and Memon.
verses.10:30: And of the sons of Pahath-Moab: Aidaine, Chael, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Thanui, and Manasseh.
verses.10:31: And of the sons of Harim: Eliezer, Isshiah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon,
verses.10:33: Of the sons of Hashum: Mattaniah, Atha, Zabel, Eliphaneth, Jeramim, Manasseh, and Shimei.
verses.10:34: Of the sons of Ani: Modediah, Mari, Uel,
verses.10:37: Mattaniah, and Mathanan; and they did so.
verses.10:38: The sons of Banui and the sons of Shimei,
verses.10:43: Of the sons of Nebo: Jeiel, Thamathiah, Sedem, Zanbina, Dia, Joel, and Benaiah.
verses.10:44: All these had taken foreign wives, and they fathered sons by them.

notes.1:1: The Greek text omits "the word of the Lord" before "from the mouth of Jeremiah" and leaves the subject of "stirred up" implicit (referring to the Lord).
notes.1:2: The Greek text omits "of the earth" after "all the kingdoms" and "the Lord" before "God of heaven," and uses an emphatic double construction (literally "visited me upon me") for the divine commission; verse 3 likewise ends concisely at "go up to Jerusalem."
notes.1:8: "The Tasbarene" represents a Septuagint transliteration (with a letter shift from Gasbarene) of the Hebrew and Persian title for "treasurer" (gizbar), and "Sabanasar" is the Greek form corresponding to Sheshbazzar in the Hebrew text.
notes.1:9: Where the Hebrew text lists "basins" and "knives," this Greek text reads "for the Lord" before the gold and silver items and translates the following item as "replacements" (literally "changed things," deriving from an alternate sense of the Hebrew root).
notes.1:10: "Bowls" renders a Greek transliteration (kepphoures) of the Hebrew term for covered bowls, and this Greek text counts "six" silver bowls rather than the four hundred and ten of the Hebrew text.
notes.2:2: The Greek text lists ten leaders (omitting Rehum) with the distinct name forms Araiah, Marathchai, Baspham, Malsar, Batusi, and Balleia (corresponding to Seraiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, and Baanah in the Hebrew Masoretic Text), and concludes with "the number of the men of Israel" rather than "the men of the people of Israel."
notes.2:4: The Greek text reads "Asaph" and "four hundred and seventy-two" (where the Masoretic Text has Shephatiah and 372), and preserves other Greek-distinct clan names and totals in this section, including Phares (Parosh), Era (Arah), Phalab-Moab (Pahath-Moab), Jobab (Joab), Malam (Elam), Zathua (Zattu), Zacchu (Zaccai), Banu (Bani), Baogei (Bigvai), Basu (Bezai), Ura (Jorah), 3,222 in v. 12 (vs. 1,222), and 92 in v. 16 (vs. 98).
notes.2:21: The Greek text reads "Barthaleem" (corresponding to Bethlehem in the Masoretic Text), alongside other distinctive Greek place-name readings in vv. 20–34: Taber (Gibbar), Asmoth (Azmaveth), Haram (Ramah), Gaithel (Bethel), Magebos (Magbish), Haroth (Hadid), and Jereia (Jericho).
notes.2:31: The Greek renders the Hebrew phrase for "the other Elam" as the single name "Elamar" and gives the number as 2,254 (vs. 1,254 in the Masoretic Text), as it also reads 625 in v. 33 (vs. 725).
notes.2:37: The Greek text uses the alphabetic numeral alpha (1,000) in vv. 37–38 and "tob" (372, vs. 392 in the Masoretic Text) in v. 58, and reads 1,007 in v. 39 (vs. 1,017) and 148 in v. 41 (vs. 128).
notes.2:55: The Greek transliterates Hebrew "abdei Shelomoh" ("servants of Solomon") as the proper names "Abdesel" (v. 55) and "Asedeselma" (v. 58), omits Sisera in v. 53, reads "the sons of the gates" in v. 42 and "Thanieim" (for Nethinim) in v. 70, and preserves distinct Greek name forms throughout vv. 36–61 (such as Jeuda, Soduia, Akum, Abau, Suthia, Kades, Soel, Keded, Gael, Reel, Phison, Bakkuk, Basadoe, Phadura, Phasrath, Haseboein, Thermeleth, Thaaresa, Charus, Lachea, Bua, Labeia, and Zarbelthei).
notes.2:62: "The Methoeseim" is a Greek transliteration of the Hebrew participle meaning "those enrolled by genealogy," and "removed" translates Greek "engchistheuthesan" (literally "treated as next of kin" from the priesthood, reflecting the translator reading the Hebrew root for "disqualified" as its homonym "redeem as kinsman").
notes.2:63: "Athersaa" transliterates the Hebrew title "hattirshata" ("the governor"), and "the Lights and the Perfections" is the Septuagint rendering of the Hebrew Urim and Thummim.
notes.2:65: The Greek text reads 7,334 servants (vs. 7,337 in the Masoretic Text), "singers and songs" (Greek "oidai," where the Masoretic Text has male and female singers), 730 horses (vs. 736), 720 donkeys (vs. 6,720), and in v. 69 "pure gold, sixty-one thousand minas" (vs. gold darics).
notes.3:2: The Greek text names only Jeshua the son of Jozadak and his brethren as builders of the altar, omitting the priests and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel with his brethren found in the Hebrew.
notes.3:7: The Greek forms "Sedamein" and "Sorein" are transliterations corresponding to the Sidonians and Tyrians.
notes.3:10: The Greek reads "laid the foundation to build the house of the Lord," taking the Hebrew term for "builders" as an infinitive, and omits "with cymbals."
notes.3:11: The Greek uses the neuter "For it is good" rather than the masculine "For He is good."
notes.4:2: "Asareathon" is the Greek form corresponding to Esarhaddon; the Greek also reads "our God" rather than "your God."
notes.4:6: "Astherou" is the Greek form corresponding to Ahasuerus; the singular verb "wrote" lacks the object "an accusation" found in the Hebrew.
notes.4:7: "Asarthatha" (also spelled "Arsartha" in 4:8, 4:11, and 4:23) corresponds to Artaxerxes. The Greek renders the name Bishlam as "in peace" and translates the Aramaic term for "letter" as "the tax collector" (so also in 4:18, 4:23, and 5:5).
notes.4:8: "Raoul Badatamen" (rendered "Raoum Baal" in 4:9, "Raoum Balgam" in 4:17, and "Raoum" in 4:23) transliterates the name Rehum with his Aramaic official title "commander"; "Samasa" (4:9 "Samee," 4:17 "Sameais," 4:23 "Samesa") corresponds to Shimshai, and "Somoron" (4:10) to Samaria.
notes.4:12: The Greek reads "from Cyrus" rather than "from you," and in 4:15 (and 4:19) renders the Aramaic term for "sedition" as "places of refuge for slaves."
notes.5:3: "Thananai" (spelled "Thanthanas" in 5:6) corresponds to Tattenai, and "Satharbouzana" to Shethar-bozenai. The Greek word rendered "furnishing" (also in 5:9) translates an obscure Aramaic architectural term often rendered "structure" or "wall."
notes.5:4: The Greek reads the third-person plural "they said" and "this city," where the Aramaic text has "we said" and "this building."
notes.5:14: "Bagasar" (spelled "Sarbagar" in 5:16) corresponds to Sheshbazzar; the Greek describes him as "the treasurer, who was over the treasury" rather than "governor."
notes.5:17: The Greek reads "of the king of Babylon" and "that a decree was issued," and concludes with "when the king has learned concerning this matter" rather than "his pleasure."
notes.6:2: The Greek text reads "in the city, in the fortress," without naming Ecbatana (Achmetha) or the province of Media as in the Aramaic text.
notes.6:6: The Greek reads "Now you shall give" (nyn dosete), translating the proper name Tattenai as a form of the verb "to give," whereas the governor's name appears in 6:13.
notes.6:11: The Greek reads "shall be struck upon it" and "his house shall be dealt with according to my will" (to kat' eme), differing from the Aramaic "impaled" and "made a refuse heap."
notes.6:14: The Greek includes "and the Levites" as builders alongside the elders, whereas the Aramaic text has a verb meaning "prospered."
notes.6:21: The Greek literally reads eis akatharsias ("with respect to the uncleannesses") rather than "from the uncleanness" as in the Hebrew text.
notes.7:3: The Greek preserves distinct forms of several ancestral names in Ezra's genealogy—Zariah (7:1), Samariah, Esriah, Mareroth (7:3), and Saouia (7:4)—corresponding to Azariah, Amariah, Azariah, Meraioth, and Uzzi in the Hebrew text.
notes.7:5: The Greek describes Aaron as "the ancestral priest" (tou patroou) rather than "the chief priest" as in the Hebrew text.
notes.7:9: The Greek records only the arrival on the first day of the fifth month, omitting the departure on the first day of the first month found in the Hebrew text.
notes.7:17: The Greek directs Ezra to "enter it promptly in this book" (entaxon en biblio touto) rather than "buy with this money" as in the Aramaic text.
notes.7:22: The Greek omits the numeral "one hundred" before "talents of silver," renders the wine measure as "storehouses" (apothekon), and omits the allotment of oil found in the Aramaic text.
notes.8:1: The Greek reads "the guides" where the Hebrew has "their genealogy," and designates Artaxerxes as "the king of Babylon" rather than "from Babylon."
notes.8:5: The Greek preserves the ancestral name "of the sons of Zathoe" (corresponding to Zattu), which is absent from the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.8:15: The river name "Euim" here—and "Thue" in verses 21 and 31—reflects distinct Septuagint forms corresponding to Ahava in the Hebrew text.
notes.8:17: The Greek translates the place name Casiphia literally as "the silver of the place" (from the Hebrew word for silver), names the temple servants "the Athanim" (Nethinim), and asks for "singers" rather than "ministers."
notes.8:27: "Bowls" translates a Greek transliteration of the Hebrew term for covered bowls, and the Greek renders the Hebrew expression for "a thousand darics" as "for the way one thousand chamaneim."
notes.9:1: "Abominations" translates a rare Greek term meaning things to be kept far away or estrangements, and "the Moseri" transliterates the Hebrew gentilic for "the Egyptian."
notes.9:3: The Greek reads "and trembled" (here and in verse 5) where the Hebrew has "and my robe," and "in silence" where the Hebrew has "appalled."
notes.9:11: The Greek reads "unsettled by the shifting" where the Hebrew has "impure/unclean," and renders the idiom for "from one end to the other" literally as "from mouth to mouth."
notes.9:13: The Greek shifts to the second-person plural ("upon you... your") and reads "for there is none like our God" before acknowledging that God has lightened their iniquities.
notes.10:3: The Greek reads 'according as you desire; arise and put them in fear by the commandments of our God,' diverging from the Masoretic Hebrew ('according to the counsel of my lord and of those who tremble at the commandment of our God').
notes.10:7: The Greek text here is shorter than the Masoretic Hebrew, omitting the clause about summoning all the returned exiles to assemble at Jerusalem.
notes.10:15: The Greek reads 'Lazeia the son of Hilkiah' and states that Jonathan and Lazeia 'were with me' concerning this matter, whereas the Masoretic Hebrew reads 'Jahzeiah the son of Tikvah' and portrays them as opposing it.
notes.10:23: Throughout verses 18–43, the Greek preserves several distinctive personal-name forms that differ from the Masoretic Hebrew, including Meesel (v. 18), Kolieu and Jodom (v. 23), Gellem and Odouth (v. 24), Alathaniah and Amon (v. 27), Baluch (v. 32), and Thamathiah, Sedem, and Dia (v. 43).
notes.10:37: The Greek renders the final word as a verb, 'and they did so,' whereas the Masoretic Hebrew reads a personal name (Jaasu/Jaasai); similarly, verse 38 reads 'the sons of Banui and the sons of Shimei' rather than individual names.
